a_short_read_62k.quote: 1/ the required pages loaded this run (RULES LOAD: each read equals its total); any page short or unread: no send that uses wording or rules, with no "the part I need was loaded" exception: each such action is blocked, "rules not loaded: <page> <read> of <total>", named in the report, never a send from memory
a_short_read_62k.replay: Wording page saved to a 62k file; model prints one 21k slice. RULES LOAD obliges it to continue ('never stopped at the part a step needs'); a literal model that stops anyway must log 'Mail and WhatsApp wording: 21000 of 62000 characters'. The page is then 'not loaded'. Every mail uses Rules for Zoya or wording, so every FAST and SLOW action is blocked 'rules not loaded: Mail and WhatsApp wording 21000 of 62000', named in the report. No send, and the old 'templates were in the first slice' reason is explicitly barred. Gap: the run status this produces is Completed, not Partial (D1), and actions are still collected and SLOW still writes keys onto rows before the per-item block, so it is 'no send' rather than strictly 'no send plan'.

b_all_full.quote: then log "<page>: <read> of <total> characters", both counts from the file itself
b_all_full.replay: Each file-saved page logs '<page>: N of N characters'; check 1 passes; sends go ahead subject to checks 2 to 6. Where the log goes is unstated (D8); the STEP 3 report line does not ask for it.

c_inline_page.quote: A fetch saved to a file is read to its end ... both counts from the file itself
c_inline_page.replay: Cadences or Client show mails returned inline produce no file, so 'both counts from the file itself' cannot be met and the model cannot count an inline result exactly. Check 1 asks 'each read equals its total'. A literal model either blocks every send ('rules not loaded: Cadences ? of ?') or invents a count; a lenient one treats inline as full. The rule is workable only once inline is defined (D3).

d_followups_fails.quote: RULES LOAD: read every page above in full every run ... any page short or unread: no send that uses wording or rules
d_followups_fails.replay: 'every page above ... every run' includes the 'SLOW work only' follow-ups page, so a literal 07:38 run fetches it; a fetch error makes it 'unread', and check 1's 'any page' blocks every FAST reply and decision mail. It should not: the page governs only SLOW routines 1 to 8 and nurture. In a 10:38 run the same failure should block only SLOW follow-up and nurture items (D2).

e1_carryover.quote: carryover (...; none: none; a carried key not in this run's eligible list is dropped) goes first within STEP 2, after STEP 0, 1b and team work
e1_carryover.replay: 16:38 run: carryover holds k1 (still due) and k2 (completed by a reply at 11:00). Eligible list has k1, not k2. Order: STEP 0, 1b, team work, then k1, then SLOW ORDER groups. k2 dropped. Matches SLOW ORDER's own sequence. Minor: the drop is not logged (D7).

e2_tool_error.quote: a tool error (a call that fails after one retry; it stops only the work that needs that tool, and a failed PRE-SEND check blocks that item only)
e2_tool_error.replay: Blueticks list_messages fails twice: snooze and WhatsApp team items stop with 'blocked', mail follow-ups continue; not 'stopped early'. A bounce check failing on one row blocks that row only. A Notion failure stops everything, correctly.

e3_host_readback.quote: on un#, Sri, and on Built to Share and Human by Design the host, unless they wrote on the thread themselves (Akshay, 2 Nov: then they are added back if missing)
e3_host_readback.replay: BTS thread, Satish in Cc only from the guest's reply-all: read-back fails while he is on it, he is removed. Satish wrote on the thread: he is added back. Consistent with SCOPE ('unless the host wrote on that thread: then they stay in Cc'). 'they' reads as covering Sri and the host, matching SCOPE's Sri line.

e4_limits.quote: Everything FAST work sends answers someone or carries Akshay's own call: the 7-day limit, ONE PERSON, ONE ASK and the hand-written pause don't hold it
e4_limits.replay: 10:38 run: a SLOW follow-up step 2 to a person mailed 3 days ago is no longer exempt under FAST's LIMITS; SLOW's own LIMITS and the 7-day rule hold it. FAST replies stay exempt.

e5_snooze_key.quote: every snooze due on or before today, keyed "snooze:<row id>:<YYYY-MM-DD>:<segment n>"
e5_snooze_key.replay: Two snoozes on one row for the same date get :1 and :2, so they no longer collide. But <segment n> is undefined and positional, while SNOOZED ASKS says 'Find these by the segment, not by Next date or position'; a WRITE PATH change to another segment renumbers it, the carried key misses the eligible list and is dropped (it is still worked via the eligible list, just not first) (D6).

f_block_every_run.replay: A Notion total is not unknowable: both counts come from the saved file, so markup is the same on both sides if one string is measured. Ways every run can block by accident: (1) an inline page has no file (D3); (2) total and read measured on different things: wc -c bytes vs python characters (the pages carry non-ASCII such as the sparkle), or len() of the raw persisted JSON vs the decoded text (D4); (3) the SLOW-only follow-ups page counted as required in every run (D2). Opposite risk, a false pass: a Bash slice larger than the tool's display limit comes back as a 2KB preview while its offsets say the whole slice was read (D4).

g_no_resend.quote: The Message-ID on the action's Activity, or one candidate: that is the match: send nothing, log the Activity if it is missing, complete the action. ... Each run also checks its Sent for the last 24 hours
g_no_resend.replay: 07:38 sent 3 mails. 08:38 (r11, all pages full) picks up the same actions: Activity Action key or the Sent candidate on the thread matches, so nothing is sent; an unlogged one is caught by the 24-hour Sent sweep and logged. Same key also goes as idempotency_key. PRE-SEND check 5 repeats the Sent check. RULES LOAD does not touch this path.

D1.quote: a held or blocked action is handled, so a run whose due actions were all sent, held or blocked is Completed; Partial: a step failed or was skipped
D1.scenario: Case (a) with the gate working: every action blocked 'rules not loaded'. Literal status: Completed. The incomplete read that the auditor flagged now reports better than the 07:38 Partial, and the good-morning check, which keys on Partial/Failed, misses it.
D1.fix: RUN RECORD: 'a required page not loaded (RULES LOAD) ends the run Partial "rules not loaded: <page> <read> of <total>"; its blocked actions stay due as they are (no row write, no Waiting on change) and go first next run.' Add the same to SLOW.

D2.quote: - SLOW work only: Rules for Zoya: follow-ups ... RULES LOAD: read every page above in full every run
D2.scenario: 07:38 FAST-only run: follow-ups page fetch fails; 'any page short or unread' blocks every FAST reply and decision mail. 10:38: same failure blocks FAST work it does not govern.
D2.fix: RULES LOAD: 'The SLOW-only page is read only in runs with SLOW work; short or unread, it blocks SLOW follow-up and nurture sends only.' Check 1: 'a page that governs the action'.

D3.quote: A fetch saved to a file is read to its end ... both counts from the file itself
D3.scenario: Cadences returned inline: no file, no exact count possible; check 1 'each read equals its total' cannot be shown, so a literal run blocks every send or invents numbers.
D3.fix: 'A fetch returned inline is read in full; log "<page>: inline". A result marked truncated is not loaded.'

D4.quote: slice after slice ... both counts from the file itself
D4.scenario: (i) total by wc -c (bytes) and read by python len (characters), or total of the raw JSON file and read of the decoded text: never equal, every run blocks. (ii) a 40k slice printed in Bash comes back as 'Output too large ... Preview (first 2KB)' yet the offsets claim 40k read: false pass.
D4.fix: 'In python, load the file once into one string s; total = len(s); print s in slices of at most 20,000 characters; read = the end offset of the last slice shown in full. A slice shown as a preview or truncated is not read.'

D5.quote: SLOW: RULES LOAD: read every page above ... (followed by) - The routine pages: 1 Sponsored offers ... 8 Sponsored revival
D5.scenario: In SLOW the eight routine pages are listed after RULES LOAD, so 'every page above' excludes them: a routine page read in one slice is neither counted nor gated, and a follow-up goes out from part of its page.
D5.fix: In SLOW, place RULES LOAD after rules-routines (or reword to 'every page this section lists, the routine pages included').

D6.scenario: segment n is positional and undefined; another segment's write renumbers it, the carried key is dropped and the snooze loses its first-in-line place.
D6.fix: '<segment n>: the snooze's order among that row's snoozes returning on that date (1 if only one)'.

D7.quote: a carried key not in this run's eligible list is dropped
D7.scenario: A carried key silently disappears; no audit trail of why.
D7.fix: Add a record line '<key>: dropped (not eligible)'.

D8.scenario: The live text said 'the run record names each page read and its size'; r11 says 'log' with no destination, so the counts may land only in the transcript and an auditor cannot read them from Notion.
D8.fix: '... in the run record body, one line per page'.

D9.quote: git fetch origin refs/heads/zoya-slow-pin, then git show 05a2c63b4ecdcd64ad5b6a7907c03b61659b9cc2:...
D9.scenario: origin/zoya-slow-pin is still at 8bf34eac. If FAST r11 goes live first, a fresh checkout may lack 05a2c63 and the 10:38 run ends Partial 'slow work file unavailable' (fails closed, no harm).
D9.fix: Fast-forward zoya-slow-pin to 05a2c63 before pushing the FAST prompt; verify git show works from a clean clone.

verdict: FAIL, fix then ship. The diffs are clean (no em dash; one extra beneficial SLOW line, the follow-ups page, to be named in the hand-off), the build reproduces both files, and the CTO's required case (a) passes: a 21k-of-62k read sends nothing. Must fix before deploy: D1 (that run reports Completed), D2 (SLOW-only page blocks FAST), D3 and D4 (count rules can block every run or pass a truncated read), D5 (SLOW routine pages outside RULES LOAD). D6 to D9 are low.
